D006_m001.question:
It's been quite a rough year and a couple of months, doctor. About ten months ago, everything just sped up. I felt amazing, like I could finally tackle all the house projects and volunteer work I’d put off. I was buzzing with energy, starting a million things at once – redecorating the living room, planning elaborate meals, even trying to learn a new language. But then, little things would send me flying off the handle, and the next minute I’d be laughing hysterically. Every little noise or movement around the house would totally yank my attention away from whatever I was doing.

About eight months ago, things got really strange. I started hearing whispers, mostly when I was alone, like people talking about me. Sometimes it's just garbled, like "kitchen...dirty...dishes...never..." And lately, for the past three months, I've been feeling so low. It’s hard to even pretend like I want to see anyone, so I just avoid calls and texts. There are moments when I get these terrifying urges, like when I'm watching the kids play in the park, I just want to run into traffic, or standing on a tall balcony, I have to fight off a desire to jump. It’s absolutely horrifying. And then there's this persistent feeling, especially lately, that something is terribly wrong inside my body, even though all my check-ups say I'm fine. And the voices are still there, even when I'm feeling really down. It’s like a constant battle in my head.
D006_m001.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder

D006_m002.question:
"Doc, it's been a rough year, over a year now. Things started getting weird about ten months ago. I felt… invincible, you know? Like I could take on anyone, anything. I was working nonstop, taking extra shifts, starting all these new training regimes, but couldn't stick with any of them for more than an hour. My mates at work said I was too much, always upbeat, but it felt right to me.

Then, about eight months back, things got stranger. I’d feel these… crawlies, like bugs under my skin, but there’s nothing there. And sometimes, I’d blurt out words that made perfect sense to me, but everyone else just looked confused, like when I told my boss about the 'mind-gate' I discovered. It was happening even when I wasn't feeling so high. For the past three months, though, it’s all gone to hell. I've lost all interest in my workouts, in everything really. All that energy is gone, and I’ve been thinking, really thinking, about how I could just… end it. Like, specific plans, you know? It's messed up my whole routine, and I can't keep living like this."
D006_m002.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder

D006_m003.question:
It's been quite a while now, probably over a year, that things started feeling...off. I'm 42, a furniture maker, and usually I love my work, but lately, it's just a mess. For the past ten months, I've been all over the place. One minute I'm ecstatic, buzzing with ideas for new pieces, then suddenly I'm snapping at everyone, furious about nothing. I can't sit still; my workshop is full of half-finished projects because I just jump from one thing to the next, never completing anything. It’s impossible to focus, and it's really hurting my business.

Then there are these smells… for about eight months now, I keep smelling burning plastic or sometimes rotting meat, even when there’s nothing there. It’s constant and distracting. And sometimes, when I try to talk, my words just get jumbled up, like a word salad. People look at me confused, and I just stop trying.

Even when I'm not buzzing around like crazy or feeling utterly miserable, these strange things happen. There’s this guy, a client, I swear he’s madly in love with me, even though he’s never said anything. I just know it. And the smells are still there, even when my mood seems…normal.

And when I dip, which has been happening for about three months, it’s bad. My divorce already hit me hard, but now, even when I manage to get a commission done, I just don't care. It means nothing. Sometimes, I’ll be on a ladder reaching for wood, and I get this sudden, terrifying urge to just…jump. Or if I’m near traffic, I have to fight the impulse to run right out. It's truly frightening.
D006_m003.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder

D006_m004.question:
Well, doctor, for about a year now, things have been… off. It started about ten months ago, with this energy I just couldn't contain. I'd feel so wonderfully happy, just buzzing, and I'd jump from one thought to the next, like a little bird drawn to every flicker outside the window. I even started tasting things that weren't there — bitter almonds, or sometimes something metallic, for the past eight months or so. It's been quite disruptive, honestly.

Then, for about three months, I just sank. All that energy vanished. I didn't want to see anyone, just stayed in my chair, and honestly, there were days I just wished I wouldn't wake up. No plans, just a longing for peace. And these tastes, they keep coming back, along with this unsettling feeling that my insides are all wrong, twisted or decaying somehow. It’s hard to explain, but it feels so real, even when I know it can’t be.
D006_m004.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder

D006_m005.question:
It’s been over a year now, and things just feel… off. Like, since last spring, maybe ten months ago, my energy's been through the roof. I've been pulling all-nighters, sketching out lighting rigs for five different bands at once, but then I can't even focus enough to finish one. My mood swings like a pendulum—one minute I’m buzzing with ideas, the next I’m snapping at everyone.

But the voices… they started a couple of months after that, about eight months ago. They’re always whispering, sometimes saying things that don't make sense, just a jumble of words. Lately, they’ve been telling me the world is going to end, and everything’s just going to collapse. It’s hard to ignore them, even when I’m trying to set up a stage.

It gets even worse though. For the past three months, this deep dark cloud has just settled over me. Nothing brings me joy anymore. The music I used to love, the lights, even just hanging out with the crew… it all feels utterly meaningless. I even tried to… well, I tried to make it all stop. It's just hard to keep going when everything is so heavy and those voices won't leave me alone, telling me things are over.
D006_m005.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder

D006_m006.question:
"Thanks for seeing me, Doc. It's been… a long couple of years, almost two actually. Things started getting weird about twenty-one months ago. It's like, people on TV or even just strangers on the street, they're sending me messages, you know? Not directly, but in their gestures or the way they say things. And sometimes, I feel this crawling sensation on my skin, like bugs, but there’s nothing there when I look.

My energy levels are through the roof. I barely sleep – maybe two or three hours a night – but I wake up feeling totally recharged, ready to go. I start a dozen workout plans for clients, get halfway through, then jump to something else. My gym used to be my sanctuary, but now I snap at everyone, and staying focused on training someone for more than a few minutes feels impossible. It’s definitely affecting my work; my clients are noticing. All this has been happening pretty much constantly since it started. And those messages, those crawling feelings? Even when my mood isn't so... intense, they’re still there, lingering for weeks on end."
D006_m006.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D006_m007.question:
"It’s been pretty rough for about two years now, maybe a bit more. Lately, it's like my brain just won’t switch off. I used to be so focused at work, you know, with the robotics, but now I can barely concentrate on a single task for more than a few minutes before my mind jumps to something else. My wife keeps saying I'm irritable, and she's probably right. Little things just set me off, which isn't like me. And sleep? I hardly need any of it. I'll get a few hours, then I'm wide awake, buzzing with energy, feeling like I could run a marathon.

What's really getting to me though are these other things that started about a year and nine months ago. I see things, little flickers or shadowy figures out of the corner of my eye that aren't there. And it feels like everything's connected to me. When the news talks about certain tech companies, I feel like they're sending me coded messages. Or when a car drives by slowly, I just *know* they’re watching me, that something specific to me is going on. It’s hard to explain, but it’s constant, even when I’m not feeling so revved up. It just never seems to fully go away."
D006_m007.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D006_m008.question:
"Well, doctor, it's been a long haul, nearly two and a half years now, and I'm just… worn out. My husband suggested I come in. For about a year and nine months, things have been particularly tough. I've been sleeping maybe two or three hours a night, but strangely, I still feel buzzing, like I could conquer the world. At work, I'd start auditing one client, then jump to another, then suddenly decide to reorganize my entire desk – it’s a constant whirlwind of activity, and I snap so easily at my colleagues, even over the smallest things. It’s not like me.

The other thing, and it’s a bit embarrassing to say, is that I’ve been seeing things. Like, sometimes I see faint figures in the periphery of my vision, or things fleetingly shift shape. And there’s this deep conviction that my boss, Mr. Henderson, is sending me secret messages through his meeting agendas, little hints of his affection. It's a bit silly, I know, but I *feel* it. Lately, these visions and thoughts about Mr. Henderson just intensify, even when I'm feeling alright otherwise. It's all just so overwhelming."
D006_m008.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D006_m009.question:
"Thank you for seeing me, Doctor. It's… I’ve been feeling really off for almost two and a half years now, but these more intense periods, they’ve been going on for about a year and nine months. Lately, I've had this persistent feeling, this absolute conviction that something terrible is coming, like a major catastrophe, the world ending. It's not a thought I can shake. And sometimes, I smell this acrid, burning smell, like smoke, even when there's nothing there. It's startling.

Then there are these other times, also for about a year and nine months, where I feel unbelievably good, almost euphoric. I’m full of energy, like I could take on anything. I'll get so many ideas for my accounting work, staying up all night, sometimes for days, without feeling tired at all. My husband, he’s worried sick when I don’t sleep, but I genuinely don’t feel the need to. I start so many projects, getting halfway through one spreadsheet before jumping to another, then another. It’s impossible to finish anything, and it's really starting to affect my job.

And there have been a few stretches – a couple of weeks here and there – where I’m just dealing with those strange smells and that catastrophic feeling, even when I’m not in one of those incredibly energetic moods."
D006_m009.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D006_m010.question:
"It's been a rough couple of years, almost two now, I think. I started noticing things about a year and nine months ago. I've just been so on edge, doc, always snapping at people, even my agent, which is a really bad idea for an actor trying to make it. I just can't sit still, either; I'm constantly pacing, needing to do something. Sleep? What's sleep? I can go days without it and feel perfectly fine, even energized. But then every little sound, every flicker of light, just pulls my attention away, makes it impossible to focus on lines or anything.

And the taste... it's bizarre. There's this constant metallic, almost chemical taste in my mouth, like I've been sucking on old pennies. It's truly revolting, and no matter what I eat, it's there. Then there’s this nagging feeling, a deep-seated certainty that something is wrong with my insides, like my organs are slowly shriveling up. I feel it, you know? It's been happening on and off, this taste and the feeling about my body, even when I'm not buzzing with energy or snapping at people. It’s definitely messing with my auditions; I can't concentrate. It's just... a lot."
D006_m010.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D006_m011.question:
Lately, things have been… off. For about a year and eight months now, it’s like my brain has been running on overdrive, but not in a good way. I'm always on edge, quick to snap, and I feel this constant need to move, like there’s electricity just buzzing beneath my skin. Sleep? Forget about it. I can go days without it and feel perfectly fine, even great sometimes. But then every little noise, every movement around me, just grabs my attention and pulls me away from whatever I'm doing in the data center.

There's this woman… I’m convinced she’s sending me signals, you know? Like she's trying to communicate that she’s interested, even though we’ve barely spoken. And sometimes, I smell this strange, almost metallic scent that no one else seems to notice. It's been happening for over a year now, these odd smells. It's hard to focus at work with all this, even when I'm feeling unstoppable.

Then, for about five months, it’s like a switch flips. Everything slows down, and I just feel this crushing guilt, replaying every mistake I’ve ever made. I tear up over nothing, and it’s just… exhausting. It’s hard to even get out of bed those days, let alone keep up with the night shift. It feels like even my thoughts are rhyming sometimes, "door for more, why war?" It doesn't make sense, I know.
D006_m011.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D006_m012.question:
It's been almost two years since I first started feeling… off. Most recently, these mood swings have been completely draining. One minute I'm on top of the world, feeling like I can conquer anything – I'll barely sleep for days, just buzzing with ideas for sales pitches, can’t sit still for a second. Every little sound or movement around me totally grabs my attention, and I just jump from one thought to the next, making it hard to stay on track. But then, the next day, I crash. I feel so heavy, just profoundly sad, and I can't stop replaying every single mistake I've ever made at work or with my husband. It’s like a constant loop of guilt.

My husband and I used to be so good, but lately, I just *know* he's seeing someone else. I see things too, sometimes – shadows moving at the edge of my vision, or quick flashes of people who aren’t there. It’s been happening for well over a year now, even when I’m not in one of these "high" or "low" phases. It's really making it tough to do my job, let alone keep things together at home.
D006_m012.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D006_m013.question:
It’s been almost two years since I started feeling… off. I’m a nutritionist, right? So I’m all about balance, but my life feels anything but. My ex-husband, he just doesn’t get it. For about a year and a couple of months now, I've had this persistent feeling that my old professor, Dr. Evans, is madly in love with me. He sends me secret messages through food blogs, I just know it. And sometimes, I taste things that aren't there – like a bitter metallic tang when I’m drinking water. I even started saying words that just… come to me, like "nutri-flow" for a healthy diet, but no one else understands.

Then there are these waves. For nearly a year now, I’ll have these periods where I'm all over the place. My mood swings wildly; one minute I'm on top of the world, sketching out new diet plans, and the next I'm snapping at everyone. I can't sit still, constantly pacing or reorganizing my pantry at 3 AM. Sleep? Who needs it? I’ll go for days on end with barely any, and honestly, I feel completely fine, even energized. I'll start five different projects at once – a new cookbook, a blog redesign, a whole new exercise routine – never finishing any of them. It's really affecting my practice; clients are noticing.

But then, for the past five months, it’s like a switched flipped. This deep sadness washes over me, and it's constant. I feel so incredibly guilty, like I'm messing up everything and everyone around me, even for the smallest things. It’s hard to even get out of bed some days. It’s paralyzing.
D006_m013.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D006_m014.question:
It’s been a rough year and a half, maybe more. I keep feeling this crawling sensation under my skin, like tiny insects, even when there's nothing there. It started over a year ago, maybe 14 months, right around when things really started getting out of hand. And my late wife... I know she’s gone, but I can't shake the feeling she was unfaithful while she was alive. I see signs everywhere, even now.

For the past 11 months, my head's been buzzing. I get so irritable, like a coiled spring ready to snap at the smallest thing. I barely sleep two or three hours, feel wide awake and ready to go, but I can't focus worth a darn. My thoughts race, and it’s hard to keep track of what I’m saying, sometimes words just rhyme and chime, chime and time, rather than making sense. My work as a ranger has suffered; I can't patrol like I used to.

Then these last five months, it’s like a gray fog settled in. I just feel... nothing. Everything's dulled. And I keep replaying every mistake I’ve ever made, every little slight, feeling so guilty about things that happened years ago, beating myself up over them. It’s hard to even get out of bed some days.
D006_m014.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D006_m015.question:
"Honestly, doctor, it's been a rough year and a half, maybe more. My wife's noticed it too, and it's starting to really affect my work. For about the last 11 months, I've been running on fumes, feeling like I'm wired constantly. I barely sleep – maybe a couple of hours – but I wake up feeling fantastic, bursting with ideas. It's like my mind just jumps from one thing to the next, every little sound or movement around me pulls my attention. Sometimes I get incredibly frustrated, snapping at my team even over minor things at work, which isn't like me.

Alongside that, for over a year now, there have been... other things. I started feeling like I had this incredible, almost supernatural insight into the logistics of things, like I could see patterns no one else could. And I’ve been seeing things, too – fleeting figures at the edge of my vision that vanish when I look directly. The words I use sometimes feel weird, they just rhyme all the time, my thoughts connect through sounds rather than sense. It’s hard to explain. There were a couple of weeks where these strange perceptions were happening, even when my mood was relatively stable.

Then, for about five months, it shifted. Everything just felt… flat. Numb. All that energy drained away, and I felt completely useless, like I was a burden to everyone, especially my wife. It’s hard to keep up with work, and even the simplest tasks feel monumental. This whole thing makes functional impairment an understatement."
D006_m015.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D006_m016.question:
"Lately, I just haven't been myself, and it's making residency a nightmare. For the past year and change, things have felt... off. I've been sleeping maybe two, three hours a night if I'm lucky, but I wake up feeling like I’ve had a full eight. I’m constantly buzzing, you know? Like I can’t sit still, always pacing, feeling this intense need to *do* something, but then my mind just skips from one thing to the next. I can't even focus on charts for more than a few minutes before getting distracted.

It's been like this for about ten months now, and it’s truly impacting my work. I feel incredibly happy, almost euphoric sometimes, like everything is amazing, but it’s not normal, especially given the stress. And for the last eight months, it’s gotten weirder. I’m pretty sure one of the senior attendings, Dr. Ramirez, is in love with me. She gives me these knowing glances, little signs, even though she's always professional. It feels so real, like we have this unspoken connection. Sometimes, I also feel these strange crawling sensations under my skin, like bugs are there, but when I look, there’s nothing. Those weird crawling feelings and the thoughts about Dr. Ramirez have been constant for months, even when my mood isn't so high, for at least a couple of weeks at a time."
D006_m016.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D006_m017.question:
It's been… tough, for over a year now, maybe a year and a half. The longest stretch has been these surges of energy, almost like too much caffeine. I’ll start working on my thesis, then suddenly switch to cleaning my apartment top to bottom, then designing a new research project, all at once. My supervisor says I'm taking on too much, and honestly, I snap at him sometimes, or at anyone who questions me. It gets a little overwhelming, and I haven't really been able to finish anything substantial for about ten months.

But then, for eight months now, things have gotten even stranger. There’s this professor, I truly believe he’s trying to communicate his affection for me through his lectures, even though we’ve never really spoken one-on-one. I see things too, flashes of people in my peripheral vision, gone as soon as I try to focus. It's unsettling. Even when I’m not feeling that buzzing energy, these strange beliefs and visions linger for weeks. It’s like two different battles I’m fighting at the same time.
D006_m017.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D006_m018.question:
"Honestly, Doc, I'm just… tired. This has been going on for over a year now, about fourteen months to be exact. For the better part of ten months, I've had this buzzing, restless energy, like my brain is firing on all cylinders even when I want to shut it down. My creative work suffers because I can't focus on one story for more than a few minutes; my mind just jumps to the next big idea. I'll be flying high, feeling amazing, like I could write the next Pulitzer winner, but then things get complicated.

It started about eight months ago, these whispers. At first, I thought it was just my neighbors, but now I know they’re talking about me, plotting. They tell me my ex-boyfriend is still seeing that girl from the production company, even though he swears he isn't. I know he’s lying. I just *know* it. It’s infuriating when they confirm my suspicions, making it impossible to trust anyone. The voices are constant, these thoughts about him and her, making me question everything, even when I'm feeling great and my ideas are just flowing."
D006_m018.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D006_m019.question:
It's been close to a year and maybe two months now, and things just feel… off. Like, I can barely sit still at work, you know? My manager keeps noticing me pacing more than usual, even when there’s a line. I used to be so good at focusing on each customer, but lately, my mind just bounces from one thing to the next, making mistakes on deposits and withdrawals. Then there are these other things that started maybe eight months ago. I keep feeling like bugs are crawling on my skin, especially at night when I’m trying to relax, but there’s nothing there. He says I’m being paranoid, but I see the way he looks at other women, and I just know something's going on, even when he’s right there beside me, swearing he’s faithful.
D006_m019.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D006_m020.question:
"Thanks for seeing me, doctor. For the past year and some change, things have been… off. It started about ten months ago. One day I'd be absolutely buzzing, like I could compose an entire symphony in an hour, practicing violin for hours on end, then suddenly I’d feel incredibly irritable about the smallest thing. It's like my emotions are on a constantly changing dial. I’d start a new piece, get really into it, then abandon it for something else, never really finishing anything. My apartment is full of half-started projects.

More recently, in the last eight months, things have gotten a bit bizarre. I keep smelling this metallic, burning scent, even though no one else seems to notice it. And then there’s this crushing feeling, like the whole world is teetering on the brink of collapse, like all of humanity is going to be wiped out at any moment. It makes playing, everything, just feel pointless. I’ve tried to ignore it, but it’s hard when I can still smell it so strongly, and the catastrophic thoughts are so vivid. It’s making it really hard to focus on my music or anything else, honestly."
D006_m020.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D006_m021.question:
"Well, доктор, I'm not sure where to start. It's been... a long year and three months, to be precise. Things just haven't felt right.

It started subtly, maybe a year ago now, with this overwhelming sense of euphoria. I felt incredible, like I could finally tackle all those projects I put off during my nursing career – reorganizing the entire house, even looking into some of those online investments my late husband used to mention. I barely slept, sometimes going a few nights without even feeling tired, which was quite unlike me. My family said I was 'on a mission,' and I suppose I was. But then, about nine months ago, things took a turn. I started seeing things, you know? Little shadows at first, then people in the periphery who weren't really there. And this feeling... like I'm being watched, constantly. The neighbors, the mailman, sometimes even the local news, it all feels like they're talking about me, scrutinizing my every move. It's hard to explain, it just *is*.

Lately, though, these past six months especially, it's like a heavy blanket has fallen over me. I'm just… sad. Constantly. My appetite is gone, and even the smell of food makes me queasy. Sleep is a nightmare, literally, with these vivid, terrifying dreams almost every night. And talking? It's like my brain is moving through molasses. You ask a question, and I have to gather all my strength just to form a coherent thought. It’s a struggle. I know I’m not making much sense, but it’s all just… tangled up.”
D006_m021.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder

D006_m022.question:
It’s been over a year and three months now, and I just feel… off. Like, I go through phases. For about a year now, I've had these surges where I’m incredibly productive, sometimes working on three different design projects at once, barely sleeping, and feeling absolutely fantastic. I'll reach out to everyone I know, even people I haven't spoken to in ages, and sometimes I do things I probably shouldn’t. But then, for the last nine months or so, things get really weird.

I started hearing voices, usually whispers, saying my creative director, Mark, is madly in love with me, even though he's never shown it. It's distracting. My thoughts get jumbled, skipping from one idea to another in a way that doesn’t always make sense to others. And it's hard to even start basic tasks, like getting myself to go to the grocery store.

Then, for the past six months, even with the voices sometimes still there, a really heavy sadness sets in. I lose all motivation, my movements feel heavy, like I'm wading through mud. My sleep is broken and I wake up frequently. The only thing that really changes is my appetite; I find myself eating much more than usual. It’s hard to keep up with work or even my personal life when I'm swinging between these extremes.
D006_m022.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D006_m023.question:
Lately, it's been a real struggle, Doc. For over a year now, I've had these surges of energy where I barely sleep for days, maybe an hour or two, and I'm just buzzing. I pick up every delivery gig I can, sometimes even making risky bets on new routes or offering services for free, feeling like I'm building an empire, you know? My mood can swing wildly; one moment I'm on top of the world, feeling invincible, like I have some special connection to… well, things bigger than me. But then I'll snap at anyone who gets in my way.

For about nine months of this, it's gotten weirder. I hear voices, sometimes whispering instructions, sometimes just rhyming words together in my head, like "street beat, can't be beat." It's hard to focus on other people when they talk. I've been avoiding my friends; honestly, I just don't have the interest anymore, or the time, with everything I'm "achieving."

But then, for the past six months, it's like a switch flips. Everything feels numb, just empty. I’ve lost a good deal of weight because I forget to eat, and I wake up at three in the morning and can't get back to sleep, just pacing my tiny apartment. Even when I’m down like that, those voices are still there, telling me about my "gifts" or how I'm part of something special, even when the rest of me feels dead inside. It's messed up my delivery work, too; I've missed shifts because I just can't bring myself to care.
D006_m023.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder

D006_m024.question:
Lately, it feels like I'm living in two different worlds. For about a year now, there have been these stretches where I'm just… on fire. I'll be buzzing with energy, full of new ideas for the church, calling everyone I know, feeling like I barely need sleep. I’ve even found myself taking some rather… uncharacteristic risks. But my wife, she says I’m talking too fast, jumping from one thing to the next, and sometimes, my ideas just fly right off track. This has definitely made it hard to keep things running smoothly at the church.

Then, for the past six months, there are times when it all crashes down. It’s like my emotions just shut off, a heavy blanket pulled over everything. I’ve lost a good bit of weight without even trying, and all I want to do is sleep, but even then, I feel like I'm moving through molasses. It's been tough getting out of bed, let alone leading services.

For the last nine months, though, things have gotten even more unsettling. I've started seeing things, shapes in the periphery, sometimes figures, and this gnawing feeling that the world, as we know it, is teetering on the edge of destruction. It gets in the way of connecting with my congregation; I just don't feel like being around anyone anymore. There's been a period of about two weeks, during those downturns, where these visions and that awful sense of impending doom were all I experienced, even when the intense sadness wasn't quite as overwhelming. It’s like these two worlds, the super-charged me and the despondent me, collide, with these strange visions making it all so much worse.
D006_m024.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder

D006_m025.question:
"It's been a rough year and a bit, Doc. Mostly, I've had this buzzing energy, like I've had too much coffee, for about a year now. My wife, bless her heart, says I'm always on the go, barely sleeping, and when I do, I'm up and down all night. I even dropped a load of cash on some 'surefire' renovation scheme a few months back – seemed like a genius idea at the time, but now it just feels stupid. I snap at everyone, even the crew on site, and my libido's gone through the roof.

But then there are other things, for the last nine months or so. Sometimes I taste metal, or something foul, when nothing's there. And people on the TV, or even my foreman, they're talking about me, I just know it. Their words… they’re all jumbled sometimes, I can barely follow what they're saying. Honestly, I just don’t want to be around anyone anymore.

Lately, though, for the past six months, it’s like a switch flipped. I still taste those strange things, and I still feel like everyone's talking about me. But I'm just numb, you know? No feeling at all. My appetite's gone, I barely eat. And I can't sit still, I just pace and wring my hands, but there’s no point to it. It’s making it impossible to get any work done; my boss is really on my case."
D006_m025.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder

D006_m026.question:
"Well, doctor, it's been a rough year and some change, about 16 months now, if I'm precise. Things started getting... odd, roughly ten months ago. I’d be in my office, or even giving a lecture, and I'd hear these whispers, sometimes full sentences, that no one else seemed to notice. They'd just… pop in. And occasionally, I'd find myself laughing at something completely inappropriate, or saying something utterly childish in a serious meeting. My wife has mentioned it, too.

For the past nine months, I've had this unbearable restlessness. It’s like a constant hum under my skin, always needing to move, to *do* something. My temper's been shorter than usual; I snap at my students, even at my wife, which isn't me. And my libido, it’s been through the roof. It’s really put a strain on things. I’ve noticed people talking, looking at me strangely. I get this feeling that news anchors are sending me personal messages through the TV, or that certain phrases in articles are hidden codes meant for me. These voices have been particularly active during periods when I'm not feeling particularly revved up or down, just... existing. It's disruptive, to say the least; my work performance has definitely suffered."
D006_m026.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D006_m027.question:
"It's been...well, over a year now, maybe sixteen months total, that things have felt so off. For the past ten months or so, there are these smells. Like burnt rubber or something acrid, always just out of reach, but so vivid. And sometimes, I just...freeze. My wife says I stare off, unresponsive, for minutes. It’s like my mind just disconnects.

Then there’s this other side to it, for the last nine months I’d say. My energy levels are through the roof. I don't sleep much, but I don't feel tired. I'll get into these passionate lectures, only to feel utterly irritable and snap at my students moments later. My wife is worried; she says I'm like a different person. I also feel this intense, almost constant, sexual urge now, which is frankly quite disruptive. I’ve said some things in class, misinterpreted student comments, thinking they were veiled messages about me, specifically. It’s hard to focus on my research when I’m constantly analyzing everything for hidden meanings. It definitely impacts my work, and my marriage is strained. But then, for a couple of weeks sometimes, when I'm not feeling this overwhelming energy, those smells and the 'messages' are still there, even without the mood swings."
D006_m027.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D006_m028.question:
I’m a 35-year-old freelance writer, and lately, things have been… off. It started about a year and a half ago, but it’s been really bad for the past year. I divorced a while back, and I usually manage fine, but I can’t focus on my deadlines anymore. For nearly a year now, I've had this constant, buzzing energy, like I need to be doing something all the time. I pace around my apartment or wring my hands without even realizing it. Everything makes me snap; I’m so irritable with everyone.

Then there are these other things that have been happening for about ten months. I feel like something is crawling on me or brushing against my skin, even when there's nothing there. And sometimes, it’s like my body just… freezes. Someone asks me a question, and I can’t respond, or I just instinctively push back against whatever they're trying to get me to do. It’s not that I don’t want to, it’s like I can’t.

On top of all that, for the past month or so, I've had this strong feeling that a celebrity, someone I admire, is secretly in love with me. It feels so real. Sometimes, these physical sensations and the general buzzing energy happen at the same time. It’s exhausting.
D006_m028.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D006_m029.question:
Well, Doctor, it's been getting to me, this isolation. You see, being out here at the lighthouse… it’s usually peaceful, but lately, it’s like the peace has been… warped. For the past year and a bit, things have just felt off. About ten months ago, I started seeing things, shapes really, in my peripheral vision, sometimes clear as day actual people standing outside against the fog, or out on the rocks where no one could possibly be. And my body… it sometimes just stiffens up, like I'm a mannequin.

Then there’s this other side to it, especially over the last nine months. I'll feel great, full of energy, like I could fix every lamp, polish every lens, then suddenly I’m snapping at the seagulls. I’ve been working non-stop, taking on tasks I’d never normally consider, even trying to radio distant stations just to chat, which is very unlike me. But it’s not really *me*. I've found myself thinking the world's about to end, that the light from my lamp is the only thing holding back some huge disaster. It’s hard to keep up with the real work when my mind’s racing like that. Sometimes, even when I'm feeling alright, those visions still pop up for a week or two, even when my mood isn't all over the place.
D006_m029.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D006_m030.question:
It's been close to a year and a half now, and I just feel like I'm losing my grip. I'm a grad student, you know, always juggling papers and research, but for the past ten months, these voices started. They're not always clear, sometimes just whispers, but I know they're talking about me, plotting. It makes it hard to focus, and sometimes I just freeze up, like my body won't respond, and I’m stuck in one position.

Then there are these stretches, going on for about nine months now, where I'm just buzzing with energy. I'll take on so many projects, lecture notes, extra research – I feel like I can conquer the world, hardly need any sleep. But then I swing, just as quickly, to being so irritable that I snap at everyone. During these times, the voices seem to get louder, more insistent that people are trying to mess with my work, steal my ideas. It got so bad that for a couple of weeks, even when my mood was stable, the voices and the feeling of being watched just wouldn't go away. It’s making it impossible to keep up with my studies.
D006_m030.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D006_m031.question:
It's been, like, a really long time now, maybe two and a half years? Everything started feeling off a bit before that. Things got really bad about a year and eight months ago. I started hearing voices, usually commenting on what I was doing or sometimes just, like, chattering. It's distracting, especially when I'm trying to focus in class or at work. Sometimes I get really giddy, almost childlike, even when it's not appropriate, and then I just lose all motivation, can't even get myself to practice my Knife skills.

About a year and ten months ago, I started feeling like I was on top of the world. I'd be super energetic, constantly moving, pacing, sometimes I feel so restless. Thoughts just flood my head, one after another, so fast I can barely keep up with them, let alone try to make sense of what I should do next. I barely sleep, maybe an hour or two a night, but feel totally rested. I had so many amazing ideas for new restaurant concepts, I truly felt like a genius, like I was meant for something huge. I'd start a project, like sketching out a new menu, and then instantly jump to something else, like researching obscure ingredients. This is a problem, because it makes it so hard to get my assignments done.

But then, for the last ten months, it's been the complete opposite. I feel so empty, like there's nothing left inside. I’ve lost so much weight without even trying, and I have absolutely no energy to do anything. Getting out of bed feels like climbing Mount Everest. I skip classes a lot, which is terrible for my culinary program. I just feel so worthless, like I'm a complete failure as a chef and a person. It's hard to imagine ever getting my passion for cooking back. It's like the voices were always there, even when I felt "up", but they got louder when everything else crashed.
D006_m031.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D006_m032.question:
"It's been... getting close to two years now, I guess, since things started getting really off. I’m a sommelier, so I'm usually pretty meticulous, but lately, it's like my brain's trying to run a hundred different wine pairings at once. I'll get these strong whiffs of something burnt, like electrical wires, even when there's nothing there. And sometimes, I find myself just repeating what people say, almost like an echo. It's embarrassing.

Most days, though, I'm buzzing with energy. I can go days on just a few hours of sleep and still feel amazing, like I could conquer the world. I’ve started so many new projects, and I’m out every night, calling up everyone I know, even people I haven’t seen in years. But then, if someone looks at me the wrong way, or a customer asks a stupid question, I just snap. There are also times, though, for weeks or months, when I get this crushing sadness. I just cry, for no real reason. The thought of even uncorking a bottle feels like too much work, and I barely eat. My body feels like lead. I just go over and over every mistake I’ve ever made, wishing I could change things. And during those sad times, those weird smells, and the feeling that someone is watching me, they still happen, even when I'm not feeling so high and mighty."
D006_m032.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D006_m033.question:
I’m glad I could finally get an appointment. For about two years now, things have been… off. It started subtly, maybe two years ago, with these weird tastes in my mouth – metallic, sometimes like ash, even when I hadn't eaten anything. It's still happening now and then, tasting things that aren't there.

Then, around a year and ten months ago, my energy just exploded. I was barely sleeping, maybe three or four hours a night, and felt totally refreshed. My mind was racing, too, like a dozen news stories all trying to break at once. I'd initiate all these new segments and story ideas at work, often doing double the work of my colleagues. My boss loved it, but it was exhausting. Sometimes, I found myself inexplicably mirroring the gestures of the guests I was interviewing. It was bizarre.

But then, about ten months ago, this crushing emptiness set in. All that drive just vanished. It felt pointless, you know? Like all those awards and achievements didn’t matter. I’ve gained a lot of weight now too, and it’s hard to even get out of bed, let alone anchor a broadcast. I feel this overwhelming guilt, like I’m letting everyone down for the smallest things. During this time, the strange tastes continue, alongside a persistent, terrifying thought that the world is on the brink of collapse. I’ve been feeling this way for a while now, even when my mood isn’t a mess. It's like I'm stuck between these two extremes, and I don't know what's real anymore.
D006_m033.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D006_m034.question:
For the past two years and some change, things have been… really off. It started about two years ago, feeling this crawling sensation on my skin, like bugs, but there’s nothing there. It’s mostly on my arms and legs, and it makes me jump. Sometimes, I find myself holding strange positions for long periods without even realizing it, and my husband says my face is often blank, even when I’m talking about something upsetting.

Around that same time, I started feeling this incredible energy, like I could conquer anything. I was redecorating the whole house, baking constantly, even planning a neighborhood block party – way more than I’d usually take on. I’d be up for days and nights, barely sleeping, but I didn’t feel tired at all. My thoughts would just race, jumping from one amazing idea to the next. I felt like I had some special insight about the universe, like I was meant for something huge, something beyond just being a mom. I'd initiate conversations with everyone, even strangers at the grocery store, just bubbling with this need to connect. But during these times, I’d also get incredibly snappy, flying off the handle at my kids or husband over the smallest things. It's caused a lot of friction, and honestly, the house has been a bit of a mess from all my abandoned projects.

Now, though, for about ten months, I’ve been feeling so incredibly sad. I can barely get myself to do anything around the house, which makes me feel guilty for letting things slide. I just want to lie down, and even thinking feels like too much effort. My appetite has vanished, and everything feels like my fault. It’s hard to imagine ever feeling that previous burst of energy again.
D006_m034.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D006_m035.question:
"It's been... hard. For about two years now, things just haven't felt right. Sometimes I get this really strange crawling sensation under my skin, like tiny bugs are moving around, even when there’s nothing there. And then there are times I just… can't talk. The words are in my head, but they just won't come out. It's so frustrating because it makes it so hard to do my job, to really connect with my special ed students. I feel like I'm letting them down.

Other times, it’s like my mind is racing a million miles an hour, and I can't slow down the thoughts. I'm just buzzing with energy, can't sit still, pacing around my apartment late at night because sleep just doesn't feel necessary. My mood swings wildly too, from feeling like I'm on top of the world to snapping at anyone who looks at me wrong. And it sounds crazy, but I've been convinced for ages that my ex is cheating on me, even though we broke up almost two years ago and he moved away. It feels so real.

Then these past ten months, it’s a different kind of awful. I just feel so empty inside, like a shell. Getting out of bed is a monumental task, and the thought of planning lessons or even grading papers feels impossible. My appetite has gone through the roof, which doesn't help with how I feel about myself. And I can't shake this crushing guilt over everything, things that aren’t even my fault. Just thinking makes me so tired, like my brain is shutting down. It’s affecting everything."
D006_m035.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D006_m036.question:
It all started a little over a year and a half ago. Things just… changed. For about a year and five months now, my mood has been all over the place. One minute I'm on top of the world, feeling like I could run my own travel agency chain, calling everyone I know with these big plans, and the next I'm in tears over absolutely nothing. I've got this boundless energy, can't sit still, always feel like I need to be *doing* something.

And these phantom tastes… sometimes I swear I’m tasting something metallic or rotten when I haven't eaten a thing. My thoughts jump around so much, I can barely finish a sentence, and sometimes I just stop talking altogether, even though I try not to. I find myself moving in odd, jerky ways, too.

Lately, for the past three months, it’s been a drag. The energy has gone, replaced by this overwhelming lack of motivation. I just want to cry all the time, and it feels like moving through molasses. It's hard to even get dressed for work, let alone book someone a dream vacation. And those weird tastes and special messages from the TV are still happening, even now when I feel so low. It’s been really tough, especially since my divorce.
D006_m036.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D006_m037.question:
It’s been almost two years now, this…  strangeness. Mostly it’s this buzzing, a restless energy that makes sitting still impossible, especially in my shop. I’m usually so careful with my stitches, but lately, I’ve felt capable of anything, like I could sew the most intricate gown in an hour. I talk and talk, sometimes things just come out in rhymes, like "stitch and seam, fulfill a dream." It’s hard to stop. People say I’m easily angered, which isn't like me; a spilled spool can send me into a rage.

But then there are the other things, for over a year now. This gentleman, a regular customer, he’s absolutely smitten with me. I just know it. The way he looks at me, it’s not just about the alterations. And everything tastes like copper sometimes, a metallic tang that’s not there for anyone else. It gets so bad, I just shut down, can’t move, can’t speak, just… nothing.

In between, for the last three months, I’ve been so down. The shop feels too much, and I just want to be alone. Even then, my hands won’t rest; I pick at my cuticles until they’re raw. It’s exhausting, this back and forth.
D006_m037.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D006_m038.question:
It's been about a year and a half, maybe a little more, that things really started going sideways. I started noticing things about my body, a real creeping sense that my guts were turning to lead, that my blood was thickening to sludge. Nobody else sees it, but I can feel it, deep down. And the voices... they're not always there, but they pop up, sometimes whispering nonsense, sometimes shouting demands. They use words I've never heard before, strange, twisted sounds that only make sense in my head.

My shifts as a night watchman used to be peaceful, but now, I just can't sit still. My mind races, jump-starts, I pace the corridors, feeling like I could run a marathon, and the words just tumble out, one after another, like a dam breaking. I feel like I'm capable of anything, like I could solve the world's problems if I just had a bit more time. But then, it slams shut. For the last three months, I've been dragging myself through the nights, every movement feeling like wading through mud. Speaking is a chore. I just want to be left alone, which is easy enough on my graveyard shift. It’s been happening for a while now, this back and forth. Sometimes I'm up, way up, and sometimes I'm down, and the voices and feelings about my insides, they're always there, even when I'm not feeling so manic or so low. I've felt this way for a while now, even when I'm not at my worst.
D006_m038.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D006_m039.question:
"Well, doctor, it's been a long stretch, nearly two years now, that things just haven't felt right. My wife, bless her, says I've been a different man. For the past year and a half, I've had these surges of energy, like I could design a whole new bridge in a day, no problem. I'd be talking non-stop, jumping from one idea to the next, convinced I was on the verge of some brilliant breakthrough at work. But then, my mood would just flip, like a switch. One minute, I'm on top of the world, and the next, I'm so irritable I can't stand to be in the same room with anyone. It's really messed with my projects at the firm.

Lately, though, it’s gotten stranger. For the last year or so, I've started feeling these tingles, like insects are crawling under my skin. And there’s this woman, a client, I just *know* she’s madly in love with me, sending me these secret signals. Sometimes my thoughts get so jumbled, it’s like my brain is trying to speak a foreign language I don't understand, just a stream of words that don't make sense. There have been times I’ve found myself frozen in place, like a statue, even for a few minutes. And frankly, nothing brings me joy anymore. The things I used to love, like fly-fishing or a good book, they just feel… empty.

About three months ago, I hit a really low patch. I couldn't stop crying, often for no reason at all. Getting out of bed felt like moving through quicksand, and everything I did was incredibly slow. It’s hard to imagine ever feeling happy again, even though I remember those times when I was full of life. It’s all just so draining."
D006_m039.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D006_m040.question:
It's been close to two years now, this… strangeness. About a year and five months ago, things really started to take off. I felt like I was on top of the world, like I could whip up a Michelin-star meal in my sleep. My wife, bless her, said I was talking a mile a minute, bouncing off the walls, starting a dozen new recipes and then, just as quickly, moving on. I just felt… brilliant. Like everything had a secret meaning, especially the things on TV, they were talking right to me.

Then, about a year and two months ago, other things started happening. I started hearing whispers in the kitchen, judging my cuts, saying things no one else heard. Sometimes, I’d find myself copying the sous-chef’s movements without thinking, like a weird echo. I even started developing my own cooking terms, special words that just felt right, even if no one else understood them. My head just feels… foggy. And honestly, it’s been incredibly hard to get myself to do much of anything lately. The drive to cook, to even get out of bed, is just gone. For the last three months, I’ve felt completely blank, like all my emotions have been turned off. I sit there, unable to move, but inside I'm buzzing with this nervous energy, like I need to get up and do something, but can't. It's ruined my work, my marriage… everything.
D006_m040.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D006_m041.question:
*(Setting: A psychiatrist's office. The patient, a 53-year-old woman, Helen, is seated, fidgeting slightly with her hands. She speaks with a somewhat flat tone).*

"Well, doctor, it's just… I don't feel right. It's been going on for over two years now, getting worse for about a year and eight months. My husband finally insisted I come. For a while, I had this incredible energy, like I could finally tackle all the projects I’d put off. I’d talk and talk, barely taking a breath, and even at the museum, I’d be reorganizing displays at all hours, feeling like I barely needed sleep. But then that mood would just crash, or sometimes, it’s like it swings back and forth so fast I can barely keep up.

And then there's the taste. For about a year and seven months, I’ve been tasting… metal, mostly. In everything. My tea, food, even water. It’s always there. And I know it sounds strange, but I’m convinced something inside me is just… wrong. Like my organs are slowly being replaced by something else, something metallic. It's hard to explain, but it feels so real, so absolute. I used to love engaging with visitors at the museum, but lately, I find myself just… going through the motions. People tell me I look blank, like there’s nothing behind my eyes. I try to smile, to show I'm listening, but it feels like there’s a wall between me and whatever emotion is supposed to come out. And the restlessness… I can’t sit still, even now. It’s like there’s a current running through me all the time."
D006_m041.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D006_m042.question:
It’s been almost two and a half years since things really started to unravel. For about a year and eight months now, I’ve felt this constant buzzing energy, like I’ve had too much coffee even when I haven’t. I get so irritable, Dr., over the smallest things at the museum. A misplaced artifact, a colleague chewing loudly—it just sets me off. And I *have* to talk, almost as if the words are physically pushing their way out. I find myself pacing around the exhibits, constantly rearranging things, even when they don’t need it. My hands are always moving.

But what’s been truly disturbing for about a year and seven months are the voices. They're usually whispering, sometimes commenting. And sometimes, I just… I feel like giggling at completely inappropriate times, like during a serious board meeting. I’ve also completely withdrawn from my friends; going out just feels like too much effort these days. There’s this heavy feeling, too, like the entire world is on the brink of collapse, or something catastrophic is about to happen to our historical collections. The voices and these catastrophic thoughts, they’ve even been there during times when I wasn’t feeling so amped up or irritable, lasting for weeks at a time here and there.
D006_m042.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D006_m043.question:
It’s been over two years now, and honestly, I'm just exhausted. I started noticing things about a year and a half ago. Initially, it was this awful, persistent smell that no one else could detect – sometimes like burning hair, other times something utterly putrid. It was so distracting, especially at work. I'd find myself making these strange faces without realizing it, and my colleagues, even my patients, would look at me oddly. My thoughts would just dry up, making it hard to get through rounds or even just chat normally.

Then, around the same time, this boundless energy hit me. I could pull double shifts, take on extra projects, even redecorate my whole apartment in a weekend. My mind raced, and my words struggled to keep up; I'd talk so fast people would just stare blankly at me. Everything felt amazing, like I was living life in HD. But it wasn't just energy. I became convinced my boyfriend was seeing someone else, even though there was absolutely no proof. I'd check his phone, follow him, concoct these elaborate scenarios in my head.

The hardest part is when that super-charged feeling dies down. The smells are still there, and I’m still convinced about my ex, even if the rapid-fire talking stops. It’s like the world goes dim, but those other unsettling things – the smells, the strange expressions, the thoughts about him – they just… linger. It's really affecting my work and my personal life. I can't keep living like this.
D006_m043.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D006_m044.question:
"Well, doctor, it's been a long time coming. My husband finally insisted I come in. For the past two years and four months, things have been… off. It started about a year and eight months ago when I felt this surge of energy – like I could conquer anything. I'd bounce off the walls, needing to be constantly busy, renovating the house at 3 AM or emailing staff endlessly. My thoughts would race, and I just couldn't seem to stop talking; I'd interrupt people, just needing to get my words out. My husband says I became incredibly snappy, too, getting furious over the smallest things. And honestly, my interest in sex became quite intense, almost out of control. It definitely impacted my work; I was making impulsive decisions and clashing with parents and staff.

Around the same time, about a year and seven months ago, other strange things began. I started to notice a coppery, almost metallic smell, as if something was burning nearby, even when no one else could smell it. It’s still there, off and on. Sometimes I find myself making these odd gestures, like a little flourish with my hand when I pick up my pen, or holding my head in a particular way, almost unaware I'm doing it. It’s hard to get myself motivated for the usual principal duties; things just don’t feel as important.

There have also been periods, lasting a few weeks at a time, where I truly believed I was meant for something far greater than running a high school. I felt I had a special insight into the universe, or that I was destined for national leadership. These feelings would be so intense, and it felt very real, even when I wasn't in one of those incredibly revved-up states. It's all just so draining."
D006_m044.options:
A. Schizophrenia

    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

It’s been almost two and a half years now, maybe even longer, since things really started getting weird. I guess it was about a year and eight months ago when I first noticed this energy. And then there's this guy… I know he’s into me. We haven’t really talked, but I just know. I see the signs, the way he looks at me. I've been feeling these touches, like phantom hands, and it makes my skin crawl. It's gotten harder to hang out with anyone, I just don't have the interest anymore, or the patience. It's all just been… too much.

D006_m046.question:
"It's been a rough year and a half, doc. Lately, it's just been a whirlwind. For about the past eleven months, I've had this constant feeling that a particular client, you know, she’s head over heels for me. It’s in her eyes, the way she smiles, even if we never talk about it. And the smells… sometimes I get this overpowering scent of burnt rubber, even when there's nothing there. My thoughts can get pretty jumbled, like a broken record, and it's tough to make sense of what I'm trying to say.

Then there are these stretches, the last ten months especially, where I'm on top of the world. My energy levels are through the roof. I don't need sleep, just go, go, go. My studio is messy, but I feel like I could tattoo for days without stopping. I pace, I fidget, I just can't sit still.

But then, for about four months, it all crashes. There's just no joy in anything – not in my art, not in anything. I wake up constantly throughout the night, and even when I do sleep, I feel heavy, slow, like I'm moving through molasses. And the guilt… it's crushing. I feel responsible for things that aren't my fault, like I deserve whatever bad is happening. It's really hard to function when I'm like that."
D006_m046.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D006_m047.question:
It’s been over a year now, close to a year and a half, that I’ve felt… off. For the past eleven months, things have gotten really strange. Sometimes I feel like I'm bursting with energy, like I could reorganize the entire library in a single night. I get so irritable too; even a whisper feels like a shout, and I snap at people for no reason. I pace constantly, my hands just can't seem to stay still. It's like my mind is racing, and I just can't hold onto one thought. Words just keep popping out, like "book nook took a rook!" It sounds clever in my head, but I know it makes no sense.

There are these moments, for weeks at a time, sometimes when I'm feeling really energetic, sometimes when I'm not, where I see things, like shadows moving in the stacks, or even faces in the reflections of the windows, even when no one's there. I also have this deep-seated conviction that I'm meant for something much grander than cataloging books, that I have a special gift, a sort of cosmic understanding that others don't possess.

Lately, though, for the past four months, even with that strange energy, I just can't find joy in anything. My books, my quiet afternoons—they just feel flat. It takes me forever to fall asleep, my mind just keeps replaying everything. And the guilt… I feel so terrible about everything, even small mistakes at work weigh me down so much, like I'm responsible for everything that goes wrong. I used to love my job, but now it feels like a heavy cloak, and I just can't shake this feeling of pointlessness.
D006_m047.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D006_m049.question:

Then there are days, even weeks, when I just feel absolutely nothing. No joy from my favorite activities, nothing. I lie awake for hours, my mind racing, or I'm up pacing, just unable to settle. And the guilt, it's overwhelming. I feel responsible for everything that goes wrong, even trivial things. It's truly a struggle to even get out of bed those days, and those periods have lasted for about four months at a time, making it impossible to do my job properly."
